subject: sexy student project: comparing speed of STAN and JAGS

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: sexy student project: comparing speed of STAN and JAGS
parts:
Dear all,

 

Here is an extremely sexy student project. Half of the BUGS examples in our BPA book have now been translated into the other bayesian HM modeling software STAN (see http://www.r-bloggers.com/kery-and-schaubs-bayesian-population-analysis-translated-to-stan/). There are rumours about the wonderful speed of STAN compared to everything else and I think many people would be very interested to know how STAN compares with JAGS for these population analyses models speedwise (where speed has to be expressed in effective sample size per unit time).

 

I am convinced that it would be a very interesting project to take the examples in chapters 4-8 in our books and run them with both JAGS (see here: http://www.vogelwarte.ch/de/projekte/publikationen/bpa/code-for-running-bpa-using-jags.html) and with STAN (https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/tree/master/BPA). Probably that could even be written up into a useful and much-cited paper. And as a side effect, the student (or whoever does it) will become an expert in STAN and JAGS coding of these models and become a very sought-after person by his/her colleagues ;)

 

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.subject: Re: sexy student project: comparing speed of STAN and JAGS
parts:
Dear all,

I just joined this group.  Thanks to those who organized it.

Relevant to Marc's suggestion for comparisons: In NIMBLE (R-nimble.org) we have a function called MCMCsuite that automates comparison of NIMBLE, JAGS, WinBUGS/OpenBUGS and Stan (which of course needs different code files than the others).  Since NIMBLE provides a lot of flexibility to choose samplers or include your own samplers, MCMCsuite also allows comparison of multiple NIMBLE algorithms.

In our upcoming release, we have an additional function called compareMCMC that further automates comparisons and can be used to generate html comparison results pages like those shown in the comparisons here: https://nature.berkeley.edu/~pdevalpine/MCMC_comparisons/comparisons_home.html

The compareMCMC is available on our development branch (devel on our github repository) for anyone who doesn't want to wait for our next release (which should be soon, really) and I can help get anyone started if you email me.

Perry

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: sexy student project: comparing speed of STAN and JAGS
parts:
Dear Perry,

 

Thank you very much for the valuable information and for developing the powerful NIMBLE software. You know that I am excited that you chose the basic BUGS language as the model-building language in your project, because BUGS has just proven to be so extremely understandable to a lot of especially non-statistician researchers.

 

When I was throwing out that idea of a comparison of STAN with JAGS for some of the examples in our BPA book I was of course not wanting to ignore NIMBLE, but I just thought that since both the STAN and the JAGS code for them are readily available right now, somebody interested could get going such a project immediately. But since NIMBLE makes the running of generic BUGS models very easy I agree that it would be very interesting to included NIMBLE in such a comparison.

 

I am looking forward to try out NIMBLE for a couple of examples in volume 2 of our AHM book !

 

Thanks again and kind regards  --- Marc
